notes:
SIZE. 85 operators (84 gated, 1 ungated), above the 25-70 guideline. The bank has 120 failures with close to one concept per item; 78 operators are in a correct final program of a development task (76 in a newly solved bank item, seq_count_even and seq_gcd in the already solved MbppX/697 and MbppX/45). The 7 without such evidence are: seq_count_min (counterpart of seq_count_max, for MbppX/384 in regression.json), seq_divisible_by (base form of the two ternary rules for MbppX/817 and MbppX/883), four right-but-tied readings of train items (seq_first_odd, seq_first_even_odd, seq_min_gap, seq_best_distinct_pair_product) and seq_median (only in the still-wrong program of Mbpp/622). Dropping any of these 7 changes no development result. Four more operators solved an extra item each but were removed as one-task recipes (MbppX/540, 553, 621, 819), and four items that a named one-task definition would probably solve were left alone for the same reason (MbppX/656, 661, 702, 846; not tried).

MEMORY OF BENCHMARK TASKS. Every operator in the pack now comes from an item of bank_sequences.json or regression.json (the list above names the only two without an item of their own). Four operators that had no bank item and for which I also remembered that MBPP contains a task of that kind were removed from the pack before this report was written: seq_count_pairs_xor_odd/1 (pairs with odd xor; counterpart of seq_count_pairs_xor_even), seq_max_subarray_sum/1 (largest contiguous sum; counterpart of seq_max_subarray_product), seq_insert_before_each/2 (counterpart of seq_insert_after_each) and seq_bisect_right/2 (counterpart of seq_bisect_left). Two keyword alternatives that went beyond the wording of the bank item were removed for the same reason: "inversion&count|inversion&number of" on seq_count_inversions (the bank item says "adjacent swaps") and "count&identical" on seq_count_same_position. None of them was in a final program of a development task, so no result changed. Earlier in the work I had also tried and dropped, for the same reason or as unevidenced: three-argument forms of concat, interleave and count_same_position, reverse of the first k elements, count of unequal and of equal pairs, last index of a value, ratio of zeros, sum of products of all subarrays, difference of a pair, first even number, counts of positives and negatives. No held-out file was opened at any point; the memory is of the public benchmark.

HOW THE OPERATORS ARE BUILT. Every search function is the emitted template itself, compiled once and put behind a guard (see `add` in the pack), so the verified program and the shipped program cannot differ; pack_lint reports 0 defects and 0 untested. Named scans were also compared with brute-force definitions on random inputs (0 mismatches) and all programs with the bank's reference solutions on mutated inputs.

ENGINE CHANGE 1: TIES (worth four train items). Programs with equal score are ordered by discovery, and core unary operators are discovered before pack operators. A correct pack operator therefore loses whenever a core operator that the description also names reproduces the example by accident: Mbpp/415 (core best_pair_product/1 accepts two equal values, the task does not), Mbpp/763 (min), Mbpp/807 (first), Mbpp/784 (first(evens(x)) against prod(seq_first_even_odd(x)), both two named steps); MbppX/947 (len) and MbppX/953 (min) are the same case, without a pack operator. Nothing in a pack can change this within the rules (a cost below 1 would, but that option is reserved for type conversions). Evidence: (a) letting the four operators win, only for the check (a temporary cost of 0.9, removed again), gives SOLVED on the hidden tests for all four; (b) a one-line change in search() - append not m["knowledge"] as a last element of the sort key, so that a tie goes to a program containing a knowledge operator - was simulated in memory (no file changed) on this bank plus regression.json, with this pack alone and with all five packs loaded: exactly four final programs change, Mbpp/415, 763, 784 and 807, each to the program verified in (a); the other teachers' banks were not looked at. That would make this bank's train result 19 of 21 and cover 5 of the 7 items the 1.5B pipeline does not solve (now 3). The learn-operators step would be another way (core best_pair_product/1 gets a loss and the pack rule a win on Mbpp/415), but no operator_weights.json exists at the moment. Related: some core keywords are so common that their operators are named in most descriptions (index/2 and find/2 by 'find', len by 'number of', min and max by any 'minimum'/'maximum'), which is what makes these accidental programs fully supported.

ENGINE CHANGE 2: LENGTH ARGUMENTS. Many tasks pass (array, n) and their hidden tests give n < len(array): Mbpp/633 failed with a rule over the whole list and passed once the rule used x[:n]. A unary rule on the array is always discovered before a binary rule on (array, n), so a length-aware twin can never be preferred to its unary form; I therefore registered seq_pair_xor_sum as binary only. All other scans are unary and will fail such hidden tests on unseen tasks of this shape. Suggested fix: when an int argument equals the length of a sequence argument in the example, search over x[:n] as an implicit input, or prefer programs that use every argument.

RISKY OPERATORS. seq_dict_text is the only ungated one (str() of a dict, cost 0.5, applies to dict values only). Gates on common words: seq_slice_inclusive (range|between|indices; ternary, needs two valid indices), seq_each_concat (concatenat|join|combin|append|merg; two equal-length string sequences only), seq_words_all (word), seq_first_and_last (first&last), seq_copy (copy|clone; an identity, so it fits whenever the example output equals its input). seq_bisect_left also fires on "insertion point" without a side, so a task asking for the right insertion point would get the left one when its example cannot tell them apart. seq_first_to_end broke Mbpp/586 while it was gated by word pairs (applied twice it equals a rotation by two); it now needs a phrase. seq_median puts a new wrong program on Mbpp/622 in place of the old wrong one.

DELIBERATE DIFFERENCES FROM REFERENCE SOLUTIONS (outside the asserts). seq_first_to_end rotates by one (the reference of MbppX/665 moves every copy of the first value); seq_swap_adjacent keeps an unpaired last element (reference pads with None); seq_second_most_common is rank 2 of Counter.most_common (the reference re-reads the sorted counts, so ties differ); seq_longest_bitonic follows the definition (the reference of MbppX/522 over-counts after a rising step: 6 instead of 5 for [0, 1, 3, 3, 3, 6, 8, 8]); seq_max_sum_increasing has no floor at 0; seq_min_coins returns inf, not sys.maxsize, when the amount cannot be paid; seq_first_missing_positive returns 1 when 1 is missing (the reference of MbppX/34 returns -1).

OTHER. Checked together with the four other round-3 packs as they stood at the time: no name collision (all names start with seq_, helpers with _seq_), same results on this bank and on regression.json. Not solvable here: Mbpp/769 (expected value is in set-iteration order) and Mbpp/622 (hidden tests follow the reference loop on unsorted lists and arbitrary n).
